questions.prompt: What's the most one person can give a House candidate for the 2026 general election?
questions.why: The 2025-26 limit is $3,500 per election; the primary and general each count as separate elections.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
In NJ's 9th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $260K. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $2.5M.

questions.prompt: In the final 20 days, a campaign gets a $2,000 check. What must it do?
questions.why: Contributions of $1,000 or more received in the last 20 days must be reported within 48 hours on Form 6.

questions.prompt: NATIONAL NURSES UNITED FOR PATIENT PROTECTION (a super PAC) has spent $350K in CA's 7th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Groups helping Republicans have spent $3.4M in NE's 2nd District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is defense.

questions.prompt: NEW LEADERSHIP NOW (a super PAC) has spent $3.2M in CA's 4th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: A hybrid PAC can do what a super PAC can't. What?
options: Give directly to candidates from a limited account
questions.why: A hybrid PAC keeps two accounts: a limited one for contributions to candidates and an unlimited one for independent spending.
